inline_comments.comment: `normalizePath(importer.file)` is called once per node visited during BFS traversal. Since `ModuleNode.file` values originate from the builder and are not pre-normalized, on Windows each visited node pays a regex replace + posix normalize cost. For deeply connected graphs this accumulates. Pre-normalizing the module graph once (as suggested on line 9) would eliminate this repeated work.

general_comments.comment:
No test cases exercise the Windows code path that this PR introduces. All tests in `trace-changed.test.ts` use Unix-style paths exclusively (e.g. `/repo/src/Button.tsx`), so `moduleGraph.get(normalizedPath)` always finds a direct match and the fallback loop in `getModuleNodesByNormalizedPath` (lines 14–18) — the core of this Windows fix — is never reached. The per-BFS `normalizePath(importer.file)` path (line 59) is similarly untested with Windows-style values.

At minimum, add a test where `moduleGraph` keys and `ModuleNode.file` values use backslash separators (e.g. keys like `'C:\\repo\\src\\Button.tsx'` and `importer.file` values like `'C:\\repo\\src\\Button.stories.tsx'`) while `changedFile` and `storyIdsByFile` use the normalized forward-slash form. This directly exercises the new fallback logic and the per-importer normalization. Without such a test, a regression in `getModuleNodesByNormalizedPath`'s fallback would go undetected.

The `changedFile` argument received by `findAffectedStoryFiles` is already normalized by its only call site in `buildStatuses()` (ChangeDetectionService.ts lines 247/250 wrap both sets of paths in `normalizePath` before passing them). The `normalizePath(changedFile)` on line 29 of `trace-changed.ts` is therefore redundant in practice. Since `findAffectedStoryFiles` is an exported function, the defensive normalization is a reasonable API contract choice — but a short comment (e.g. `// normalize defensively in case callers haven't pre-normalized`) would clarify the intent to future readers and prevent this line from appearing as dead code during refactors.
